subject.title: [Feature]: Subagent session reuse for expert agents (avoid new session per spawn)

question: Should native `sessions_spawn` gain a core reuse/pooling API, should Teams gain a channel session-binding adapter, or should native subagent runs remain isolated with reuse limited to ACP/thread-bound sessions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent answer changes session-state semantics, tool/API surface, concurrency behavior, and channel ownership boundaries.

options.title: Design core opt-in native reuse
options.body: Add an explicit, scoped native reuse contract only after deciding TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

options.title: Add Teams session binding first
options.body: Implement Teams through the channel session-binding adapter seam and leave ordinary native `mode="run"` isolated.

options.title: Keep native runs isolated
options.body: Document ACP resume and thread-bound sessions as the supported reuse paths and close native run reuse as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design core opt-in native reuse
recommendation.body: Add an explicit, scoped native reuse contract only after deciding TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest feature-history signal across the original `sessions_spawn` tool, current subagent spawn path, and session-state docs.
